title: Review of the named-track moat cut on fresh seed 5: the deepest labkit body (track 24, generation 3; this seed reaches only generation 3) dies by t=25025 under the moat while its neighbour and the 17 outside bodies stay; 4 of 4 targets die
summary: The low-noise layered CIPS world unchanged, seed 5, labkit pack to t=25000 (14 persistent splits, 0 merges, max generation 3, 18 bodies). From the t=25000 state I branched a fed twin and moat arms (kF=0 in 0.6x nearest-neighbour disk, F=0 in 16 px <= r <= that radius; the finding's cutmany.py with CUT_AT) at labkit's final centroids of track 24 (generation 3, (118.0, 122.8), 183 px) and track 6 (generation 1, 185 px): each is gone (area 0) by t=25025 while the other keeps its fed size (188-191 px) and 17 outside bodies survive to t=25975; the fed twin keeps all 18. Two further far-neighbour targets (far_s5) die by t=25025 and t=25050. The finding replicates for the deepest body on a fresh seed, but on this seed the deepest generation is 3, not 4.

observations.E: gen3cut_s5.json: track 24 (generation 3) and track 6 at area 0 by t=25025, the other named body 188-191 px, 17 outside bodies kept, fed twin 18; far_s5.json: 2 more targets dead by t=25050

seeds_run.result: pass: 4/4 moat targets dead within 50 t, neighbours kept; deepest generation on this seed is 3

controls_run.E: gen3cut_s5 fed twin and the other named body; far_s5 (two more targets with fed twin)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; it reaches generation 3, so I cut a generation-3 body, not a generation-4 one. Same moat geometry and cut time as the finding; the moat is an imposed sink.
